newsitem.title: UK: IPE oil futures continue little changed, eye U.N.
newsitem.headline: IPE oil futures continue little changed, eye U.N.

text.p: IPE Brent crude and gas oil futures were little changed in light volume trade by the midsession on Monday, but Brent crude could drift down to test the $18 mark, traders said.
By 1223 GMT, the September Brent contract was trading two cents higher at $18.14 a barrel, with the front month gas oil contract 25 cents lower at $163.25 a tonne.
"We could see a test of the bottom end of the range without too much panic," Fenella Graham at Mees Pierson said. But she said the market was likely to remain restricted between $18 and $18.30.
Brokers said the imminent "rubber stamping" by the U.N. of the Iraqi oil sale deal was expected to cause few ripples in the market.

However, GNI Research said in a report that while the green light for the oil sale was fully expected by the market, the fact that the go-ahead could mean Iraqi oil shipments in the next couple of weeks meant there should still be a reaction.
"Perhaps the most bearish aspect of the Iraqi deal is the need to compress $1 billion worth of sales into a 5-6 week period," they said.
Ahead of the NYMEX open, Graham said she expected WTI crudes to move sideways.
"We're back in the range on WTI, so we can come down relatively easily to test $19.20," she said, but added it was undecided if there would be a break at the bottom of the range.
